name: Mill Creek / Avon — Existing Goodwill Store

meta.sourceModel: Basic property pull only, benchmark/reference card — per B. Blackburn 8/19/26, economics and scenarios intentionally left off pending further direction.

thesis.v: Goodwill's existing store and donation center at 34 Mill Creek Dr, south of the Charlottesville city line — this card exists purely as the comparison Jackson Green (Goodwill CFO) asked for in the 8/19 email thread, and as the reference point for cannibalization risk against the 5th Street and Pantops expansion candidates. Avon St Ext at Mill Creek carries 11,000–12,000 ADT, about 70% lighter than 5th Street SW's 19,000 ADT — the direct answer to Jackson's question. This store sits inside the 5th Street site's trade area (1.6 miles apart) but well outside Pantops' (3.6 miles), so cannibalization risk reads meaningfully higher for a 5th Street expansion than for Pantops. Not itself a deal under evaluation — no financing model or development scenario applies here.

flags.text: This is the comparison Jackson Green asked for: Avon St Ext at Mill Creek carries 11,000–12,000 ADT versus 19,000 ADT on 5th St SW at the Carter Bank site — 5th Street is roughly 70% heavier.

Address ambiguity worth resolving before this goes to Peter: geocoders place 34 Mill Creek Dr toward the Route 20 (Scottsville Rd) end of Mill Creek Drive, not the Avon St end — if that's wrong, the relevant arterial count changes. Mill Creek Drive's own frontage is low-volume either way (1,500–2,600 ADT); the store's real traffic exposure comes from whichever arterial (Avon St Ext or Route 20) it's actually closest to.

Highest one-mile median household income of the three sites ($112,758) and the only one that is majority owner-occupied inside a mile (59%) — a favorable donation-supply profile for this existing store.
Smallest one-mile population of the three sites (4,222) — note the one-mile ring here captures only two block groups, so this is the least precise of the nine ring estimates across all three cards.

1.6 miles from the 5th Street site and 3.6 miles from Pantops — the 5th Street site sits inside this store's existing trade area, Pantops largely does not. Read this as a stronger cannibalization concern for 5th Street than for Pantops.

extras.label: Why this card exists
extras.text: Not a deal under evaluation — this is a benchmark/reference card for the 5th Street and Pantops expansion analysis, built to directly answer Jackson Green's (Goodwill CFO) 8/19 request to compare 5th Street traffic against "counts on Avon at Mill Creek." Economics, rent, and scenario analysis are intentionally excluded, as with the other two cards.

extras.label: Demographic methodology note
extras.text: Ring demographics (ACS 2019–2023 5-year estimates) are aggregated by block-group centroid falling inside each radius — block groups aren't split at the ring boundary, so small rings are approximate. Median household income is a household-weighted average of block-group medians, not a true ring median.
